purpose: V5 modular-texture art direction iteration after V4 exceeded the estimated tile budget; test repeated material motifs and 8x8 tile economy
prompt: Create a new ORIGINAL tile-economical pixel-art pass over the reference: preserve its exact wide 640:224 panoramic composition and major shapes (moon, clouds, distant mountains, central Japanese castle, continuous rampart, wood rail and fight floor) while keeping the visual richness and crafted material forms. This is a Mega Drive background tileset source, so remove random microtexture and noisy one-off pixels. Make the stone wall from a small set of 8x8 and 16x16 block motifs repeated with deliberate variation; make the wooden floor from 4-6 reusable slab/edge motifs; make roof tiles from a few repeated clusters. Keep irregularity in silhouette and lighting, not in every tile interior. Design at 640x224 native logical pixel scale, crisp square pixels, no antialiasing, no smooth gradients, no blur. Maximum 8 flat visible colors with broad value groups: deep navy, two cool blue-violets, muted stone, pale moonlight, and limited rust-orange lantern/wood accents. Strong readable castle silhouette and a quiet playfield behind two fighters; top 56 pixels remain visually quiet for HUD. No characters, interface, text, logos, watermark, or realistic photographic texture. Preserve a high-end 1990s arcade pixel-art feel with repeatable texture modules. Concept art only; do not claim hardware compliance.
